skills.name: Cameroon in CEMAC: membership, geography and cooperation

note.text: CEMAC links Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. It is not identical to all Central Africa, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo is not a CEMAC member. Its treaty was signed in 1994, following earlier regional cooperation through UDEAC. Economic integration and monetary cooperation are connected but distinct. Common institutions and rules aim to improve regional links; their existence does not prove that every practical barrier has disappeared.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify the regional scope and distinguish economic from monetary integration. Builds on: international economic links and post-independence institutions. Leads to: obstacles to regional integration and wider organisations.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Cameroon’s coast and transport links can connect inland neighbours with maritime routes. Chad and Central African Republic are landlocked; the other listed members have Atlantic coasts. BEAC provides the common monetary framework. A common currency is different from a completed common market or a guarantee that every road and border procedure works without difficulty.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.
